title: Canonical Identity Beats More Content
seoTitle: Personal SEO: Reconcile Profiles, Domains and Résumés
subtitle: Resolve conflicting biographies before publishing another version.
seoDescription: Align your canonical website, résumé and public profiles using a reconciliation log, clear sameAs criteria and dated historical records that remain accurate.

artwork.alt: Monochrome editorial artwork showing one canonical identity connected to controlled public records.
artwork.label: Canonical identity / entity graph
artwork.caption: A maintained person record aligns the site, resume, profiles, and historical references.

author: SULAYMAN BOWLES
thesis: Assign one maintained profile as the source of current facts. Controlled pages should agree with it; historical records should remain clearly dated rather than being rewritten as present-day biographies.

conclusion.title: Maintain the facts, not more copies
conclusion.content: Measure agreement across important, controllable records and their links to the maintained profile. Keep accurate history dated and third-party discrepancies visible. Consistency does not force another platform to update or a search system to accept an identity claim.

evidenceBoundary: This playbook improves consistency among controlled and observable profiles. It cannot force third-party platforms to update, remain public, or be interpreted as identity evidence by a search system.
content: Your portfolio, résumé PDF, university biography, GitHub, LinkedIn, competition account, old domain, and copied speaker bio can describe different versions of you. Conflicting roles, employers, dates, project ownership, and official websites leave the identity unclear.

Reconcile these records before expanding them. Choose which controlled profile owns the current biography, experience, and education; classify supporting and historical pages; then decide how to repair stale URLs. More copies cannot settle an unresolved source of truth.

sections.title: Inventory the identities already in public
paragraphs: Collect the preferred site, HTML résumé, public PDF, GitHub, LinkedIn, portfolio accounts, institutional biographies, programs, press, and abandoned domains. Compare name, headline, employer, education dates, project ownership, and preferred homepage.

Assign a role: canonical biography for the present, supporting profile for corroboration, historical page for a dated event, or stale controlled page needing repair. Private, deleted, and weakly matching profiles remain unresolved rather than assumed equivalent.

sections.title: Align the host and the current facts
paragraphs: Resolve protocol and hostname variants consistently. Permanently redirect duplicate hosts and retired controlled routes with clear destinations. Align redirects, canonicals, sitemaps, and internal links so one signal is not asked to overcome contradictory routing.

Maintain an approved set of facts for home, About, résumé, and metadata: current work, relevant projects and institutions, and inspectable proof. Wording can vary; identity and factual meaning should agree.

sections.title: Check identity before adding sameAs
paragraphs: Use four core checks: the destination unambiguously represents this person, functions as their profile or homepage, is publicly inspectable, and contains no material contradiction. Apply this rubric before adding a URL to Person markup, then keep it maintained.

A mention is not a profile. Articles, programs, employer pages, repositories, and schedules can support visible citations, subjectOf relationships, project markup, or editorial context without asserting identity equivalence.

table.caption: sameAs eligibility rubric
rows: The destination unambiguously represents the same person
The name is shared or the connection is inferred
A reviewer can inspect the profile without privileged access
The page is private, deleted, blocked, or empty
Core current facts do not materially conflict
Employer, role, location, or ownership is misleading
The destination is a profile or official homepage
The destination merely mentions the person
The link is reviewed and still expected to persist
The account was abandoned or transferred

sections.title: Maintain HTML and reconcile the portable PDF
paragraphs: Use the HTML résumé as the maintainable website record. Semantic headings, current project links, profile details, and a modification date make it easier to update and connect to the rest of the site.
Keep PDF for applications and offline sharing, with one stable public URL. Redirect obsolete controlled filenames and reconcile visible facts before leaving another dated copy publicly available.
bullets: Treat the HTML route as the current, maintainable experience and education record.
Publish one stable PDF URL rather than creating a new public filename for each revision.
Check that the visible PDF facts match the HTML record before release.
Redirect known retired filenames instead of allowing silent duplicate copies.
Keep private application variants outside the public web surface.

sections.title: Prioritize the records you can change
paragraphs: Start with likely reviewer touchpoints: preferred website, LinkedIn, GitHub, then major portfolio accounts. Institutional and event records may belong to another owner. Log correction requests and preserve accurate historical context.

Track uneditable discrepancies rather than pretending they are fixed. A stale third-party title is a dependency; the same stale title on your site is directly repairable. Ownership determines the next action.

Current role, canonical website, project ownership

sections.title: Reconcile after changes and each quarter
paragraphs: Review after roles, graduation, launches, domain moves, and public résumé revisions. Quarterly checks catch expired links, copied biographies, renamed accounts, and newly indexed files. Record observations and actions instead of giving a profile permanent “done” status.

Measure the share of important controlled records that agree on current identity and reference the maintained source. Historical descriptions may differ because they document other times; accurate history is not an inconsistency to erase.
bullets: Review controlled profile pages and the public PDF every quarter.
Recheck redirects and canonical host behavior after deployments or domain changes.
Validate sameAs destinations before adding them and after username changes.
Record third-party correction requests separately from edits you directly control.
Keep dated historical sources when they are accurate for their original context.
